title:
Redwood + VeritasMed
	Security & Data Handling Review
summary: Redwood AE + SE reviewed security posture and data handling guarantees with VeritasMed security and privacy team. Primary asks: confirm that customer prompts/content are not used to train models, clarify retention windows for transcripts and logs, KMS/HSM support for keys, RBAC and SSO integration specifics, audit log granularity and export, and options for private deployments or dedicated pools for PHI workloads. Agreed to share SOC 2 report, data flow diagram, and sample contract language; schedule a short follow-up to walk through the SOC 2 and the encryption key flow.
action_items: Alex Chen - Share SOC 2 attestation and security whitepaper by 2026-12-03
Priya Nair - Provide data flow diagram and sample audit log export within 3 business days
Priya Nair - Confirm KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer-managed keys) and send notes by 2026-12-06
VeritasMed - Provide their compliance checklist and preferred contract language by 2026-12-08
next_steps: Redwood to email SOC2 + ISO artifacts and security whitepaper
Schedule 30-min follow-up to review SOC2 controls and key management flow (tentative 2026-12-07)
Customer to decide if they want a Dedicated pool POC for PHI testing
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CISO - VeritasMed), Sam Patel (VP Eng), Maria Gonzales (Privacy Counsel)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for making time, appreciate it. Quick agenda — go through our SOC 2/ISO posture, key things like RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/K M S integrations, and then specifically the data handling questions around prompt retention, training, PII/PHI, stuff like that.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Great, yeah we — we mainly want to be sure that nothing sent to the hosted API is used to train models, and then, you know, retention windows, who can see logs, that sort of thing. Maria will lead on privacy questions.
[00:32] Maria Gonzales: Hi, yes thanks. Two big things for us: 1) confirm no training on customer data, 2) clarify how long transcripts and raw logs are kept, and whether we can enforce deletion.
[00:45] Alex Chen: Totally. High level — Redwood's platform offers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For hosted we have a default retention policy and a contractual commitment for entitlements. For dedicated/private deployments, you control the keys and retention more directly. Priya, do you want to give a short on KMS and key management?
[01:05] Priya Nair: Sure. Quick note — we support customer-managed keys via AWS K M S and GCP K M S today, and H S M integrations for on-prem. For hosted, keys can be customer-owned (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed. If you bring your own key we never see plaintext at rest — decryption happens in a customer-controlled flow. There's an option for a private control plane for regulated workloads.
[01:30] Sam Patel: When you say "we never see plaintext" — what about logs and traces? Like request/response payloads that show up in audit logs.
[01:40] Priya Nair: Good question. Audit logs can be configured — we have different levels: metric-only, metadata-only, and full payload retention. Metadata-only includes token counts, latency, model used, route IDs; full payload contains prompts/responses. For hosted customers who need no retention of PII/PHI we recommend metadata-only plus dedicated pool or private deployment.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: So if we use hosted but choose metadata-only, are there any transient stores where payloads could be used for ops or debugging?
[02:14] Alex Chen: There are ephemeral operational caches for request processing — KV caches, batching queues — those are ephemeral and not used for training. Our policy is that customer data is not used to train models. We maintain an internal policy and contractual language to that effect. Priya, maybe pull up the exact clause?
[02:33] Priya Nair: Yeah, clause is in our security whitepaper. Short version: Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to train models unless explicitly opted in by the customer via a separate data-sharing program. There's a logging pipeline for operational telemetry but training datasets are separate and have a strict vetting process.
[02:52] Maria Gonzales: Ok, can you provide that exact language and also any pen-test reports? We need to show auditors.
[02:58] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 and relevant pen test summaries.
[03:05] Sam Patel: About RBAC and SSO — we run SAML-based SSO enterprise-wide. How granular is the RBAC in the console and API access?
[03:14] Priya Nair: We integrate with SAML/SCIM for provisioning. Role model supports Organization Admin, Project Admin, Dev, Observer. You can restrict by route and model, and also set token scopes for API keys, e.g., generation-only, embeddings-only, or admin. Audit trails show who issued keys and when.
[03:33] Jordan Lee: Is there support for session recording or just event logs? We need to keep logs for a year for compliance.
[03:40] Priya Nair: Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM — CloudWatch, Stackdriver, Splunk — and we support retention policies on the export side. Internally we keep high-fidelity logs for 90 days by default, with longer retention options under enterprise contracts. Exporting to the customer's bucket gives you control for long-term retention.
[04:01] Maria Gonzales: Encryption — we'd like to use our KMS and H S M. Also need to see how key rotation works and whether Redwood ever has access to the keys.
[04:10] Priya Nair: If you bring your own key, Redwood does not have access to the private key material. We support key rotation via standard KMS APIs; rotation is seamless as long as the new key is in the KMS and permissions updated. For on-prem/private deployments, keys stay in your HSM.
[04:25] Sam Patel: On the training/no-training front — is the "no training" guarantee auditable? Like can we get attestations that no data was exfiltrated to training stores?
[04:35] Alex Chen: We can provide SOC 2 type II reports which cover controls around data segregation and training pipeline restrictions. For additional assurance we can sign addenda in the contract that explicitly forbids training on your data; we've done that with other enterprise customers.
[04:52] Jordan Lee: Good. Two technical follow-ups: 1) can we run a short POC where we send PHI-flavored prompts to a dedicated pool to confirm no retention? 2) We need the format of the audit logs (schema) so our compliance team can ingest.
[05:05] Priya Nair: Yes on both. For POC we usually spin up a dedicated GPU pool with guaranteed isolation and configure audit logs to metadata-only and also route logs to your S3. We can also provide a scrubbed sample log. Schema is JSON with timestamp, actor_id, route_id, model_id, token_count, latency_ms. If you need full payload we mark that in the schema but warn about PII.
[05:30] Maria Gonzales: About prompt retention and the "right to be forgotten" — can you delete customer prompts on demand and do you have an API for deletion?
[05:38] Priya Nair: Yes, we have a deletion API that can remove stored payloads from the audit log store and backups in accordance with our SLA. Note that for hosted customers there's a contractual process; for private/dedicated you can delete via your own controls faster. Deletion from backups is scheduled but we can agree contractually on timelines.
[05:58] Sam Patel: Great. Any third-party subprocessors we should know about? Logging vendors, cloud providers?
[06:05] Alex Chen: We primarily run on major cloud providers and use logging/observability vendors — details are in the security whitepaper. We'll include the list of subprocessors in the doc pack.
[06:14] Jordan Lee: ISO — do you maintain ISO 27001?
[06:18] Alex Chen: We're in the process of ISO certification and can share evidence of controls; SOC 2 Type II is available now.
[06:26] Maria Gonzales: Can you clarify who within Redwood has access to customer payloads for debugging? Is that ticketed and time-limited?
[06:34] Priya Nair: Access is strictly role-based. Engineering access to payloads requires an internal approval flow (JIRA ticket), is audited, and is time-limited. We also can disable payload viewing for your organization if you prefer.
[06:50] Sam Patel: If we want to ensure no training, and no human can see payloads, what's the recommended setup?
[06:57] Priya Nair: Best is Dedicated pool with customer-managed keys, metadata-only audit logs exported to your bucket, and SSO + strict RBAC. For the highest assurance, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) removes Redwood control plane access.
[07:15] Jordan Lee: For contract language — we want explicit: "Notwithstanding any other terms, Redwood will not use Customer Data to train models without explicit written consent" + deletion SLA.
[07:26] Alex Chen: We can add that as an addendum; we'll share sample language.
[07:32] Maria Gonzales: Also want to see the data flow diagram showing where prompts touch Redis/KV caches, how long they're in memory, and whether they're logged.
[07:40] Priya Nair: We'll include a diagram and call out ephemeral caches. Typically KV caches are in-memory per instance and persisted only for warm starts; they're not included in training datasets. We'll annotate lifespans.
[07:54] Sam Patel: Small nit — you mentioned training datasets are separate — how do you ensure that debugging data doesn't accidentally make it into training? Any gating?
[08:03] Priya Nair: Training pipelines are isolated, gated by access controls and explicit approvals. There's an auditable process that requires product and legal signoff to include any external data.
[08:13] Jordan Lee: Ok, sounds good. Any more items from our side?
[08:17] Maria Gonzales: Please include the exact wording for "no training" plus the deletion API doc and retention timelines.
[08:25] Alex Chen: We'll send those. We'll also share SOC 2 and a short sample log schema and the data flow diagram.
[08:33] Sam Patel: One operational question — in the event of an incident, how fast do you notify customers and what's the SLA?
[08:40] Alex Chen: We have incident response commitments in the contract and standard notification timelines: 24 hours for high severity by email and Slack if configured. For Dedicated customers we have an on-call channel.
[08:52] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[09:00] Alex Chen: Recap — Redwood sends SOC2 and security whitepaper, data flow diagram, sample audit log schema, and contract language for the "no training" addendum. Schedule follow-up week of Dec 7 to walk SOC2 and key management. Customer to review and confirm POC needs for Dedicated pool.
[09:20] Maria Gonzales: Thanks, that works.
[09:24] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs.
[09:28] Meeting ends.
